# Network Analysis Advanced {.center}

## Topics Covered

- Community detection algorithms
- Centrality measures visualization
- Network statistics
- Dynamic networks
- Bipartite networks

Goal: Advanced network insights

## Setup

Data: 20 providers and 74 referral links between them, January to June (`data/Healthcare_Network_Dataset.xlsx`, simulated).

```{r}
#| echo: true
library(readxl); library(tidyverse); library(igraph); library(ggraph)
providers <- read_excel("../../data/Healthcare_Network_Dataset.xlsx", sheet = "Providers")
referrals <- read_excel("../../data/Healthcare_Network_Dataset.xlsx", sheet = "Referrals")

edges <- referrals |> transmute(from = FromProvider, to = ToProvider, weight = NumReferrals, Month, ReferralType)
nodes <- providers |> transmute(name = ProviderID, label = sprintf("P%02d", ProviderID), Specialty, Region)
net <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = nodes)
```

## Community Detection

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Network of 20 providers drawn with a force-directed layout, each node coloured by the community the Louvain algorithm assigned it to and labelled with its provider code."
set.seed(42)
communities <- cluster_louvain(as_undirected(net, edge.attr.comb = list(weight = "sum", "ignore")))
V(net)$community <- factor(membership(communities))
ggraph(net, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight), alpha = 0.25, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_node_point(aes(colour = community), size = 5) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = label), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.3, 2), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Community") +
  labs(title = "Provider communities (Louvain)") +
  theme_void()
```

Louvain groups providers who refer **more to each other than to the rest**; the groups can change with the random
seed, so treat them as a hypothesis, not a fact.

## Centrality Measures

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Provider network in a Kamada-Kawai layout with node size showing betweenness centrality and node colour showing degree."
V(net)$degree <- degree(net, mode = "all")
V(net)$betweenness <- betweenness(net, normalized = TRUE, weights = NA)   # weights would be read as distances
ggraph(net, layout = "kk") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = betweenness, colour = degree)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = label), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  labs(title = "Provider centrality", subtitle = "Size = betweenness | Colour = degree") +
  theme_void()
```

**Degree** = how many links; **betweenness** = how often a provider sits on the shortest path between two others
(a broker: if they are absent, referrals take longer routes).

## Network Statistics Table {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true
stats <- tibble(
  Metric = c("Providers (nodes)", "Referral links (edges)", "Density", "Mean path length",
             "Clustering coefficient", "Modularity of the communities"),
  Value = c(vcount(net), ecount(net), round(edge_density(net), 3), round(mean_distance(net, weights = NA), 2),
            round(transitivity(net), 3), round(modularity(communities), 3)))
knitr::kable(stats)
```

**Density** = links present / links possible. A **modularity** near 0 means the communities are weak.

## Bipartite Network

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Two-row bipartite network: the 20 referring providers in one row and the three referral types (routine, follow-up, urgent) in the other, with links weighted by the number of referrals."
bip <- referrals |> group_by(from = sprintf("P%02d", FromProvider), to = ReferralType) |>
  summarise(weight = sum(NumReferrals), .groups = "drop")
bp_net <- graph_from_data_frame(bip, directed = FALSE)
V(bp_net)$type <- V(bp_net)$name %in% bip$to                 # TRUE = referral type
ggraph(bp_net, layout = "bipartite") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_node_point(aes(colour = type), size = 4) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), size = 2.5, vjust = -1.2) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#2C5F8D", `TRUE` = "#E67E22"),
                      labels = c("Provider", "Referral type"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Who sends which kind of referral") +
  theme_void()
```

Two kinds of node, and links only **between** kinds: providers and the referral types they send.

## Dynamic Network (Time-based)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Two network panels with the same node positions: referrals in January to March and in April to June."
library(patchwork)
set.seed(1)
coords <- create_layout(net, layout = "fr")[, c("x", "y")]        # same positions in both panels
half <- function(months, title) {
  sub <- subgraph_from_edges(net, E(net)[Month %in% months], delete.vertices = FALSE)
  ggraph(sub, layout = "manual", x = coords$x, y = coords$y) +
    geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.4) + geom_node_point(colour = "#2C5F8D", size = 2.5) +
    labs(title = title) + theme_void()
}
half(c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar"), "January–March") + half(c("Apr", "May", "Jun"), "April–June")
```

**Fixing the node positions** makes the two periods comparable: only the links change.

## Summary

**Advanced network techniques:**

1. Community detection - find clusters
2. Centrality measures - identify key nodes
3. Network statistics - quantitative metrics
4. Bipartite networks - two node types
5. Dynamic networks - temporal changes
